Narcissus (plant) :: Uses :: Commercial uses :: part 02 :: chunk_0034
Bulbs are harvested for market in the summer, sorted, stored for 2–3 weeks, and then further disinfected by a hot (43.5 °C) bath. This eliminates infestations by narcissus fly and nematodes. The bulbs are then dried at a high temperature, and then stored at 15.5 °C.[[6]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHanks2002[httpsbooksgooglecombooksid4_kH_BffGDgCpgPA1_Hanks,_"The_biology_of_''Narcissus''"],_pp._1–29-7) The initiation of new flower development in the bulb takes place in late spring before the bulbs are lifted, and is completed by mid summer while the bulbs are in storage. The optimal temperature for initiation is 20 °C followed by cooling to 13 °C.[[7]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEOkuboSochacki2012[httpsbooksgooglecombooksid5B-ucdbgA3wCpgPA104_104]-8)

Traditionally, sales took place in the daffodil fields prior to harvesting the bulbs, but today sales are handled by Marketing Boards although still before harvesting. In the Netherlands there are special exhibition gardens for major buyers to view flowers and order bulbs, some larger ones may have more than a thousand narcissus varieties on display. While individuals can visit these gardens they cannot buy bulbs at retail, which are only available at wholesale, usually at a minimum of several [hundredweight](/wiki/Hundredweight "Hundredweight"). The most famous display is at [Keukenhof](/wiki/Keukenhof "Keukenhof"), although only about 100 narcissus varieties are on display there.

There is also a market for forced blooms, both as cut flowers and potted flowers through the winter from Christmas to Easter, the long season requiring special preparation by growers.

Fortune Global 500 :: Methodology :: chunk_0001
Until 1989, it listed only non–[United States](/wiki/United_States "United States") industrial corporations under the title "International 500" while the [*Fortune* 500](/wiki/Fortune_500 "Fortune 500") contained and still contains exclusively United States corporations. In 1990, United States companies were added to compile a truly global list of top industrial corporations as ranked by sales. Since 1995, the list has had its current form, listing also top financial corporations and service providers by revenue.

Several inconsistencies exist in *Fortune*'s ranking of cities with the most *Fortune* 500 headquarters. On June 3, 2011, the *[Atlanta Business Chronicle](/wiki/Atlanta_Business_Chronicle "Atlanta Business Chronicle")* stated examples of *Fortune* including regional headquarters for some cities, excluding regional headquarters for other cities and in some cases excluding headquarters that are physically located inside a city limit.[[1]](#cite_note-1)

Since 2001, there has been significant change in the geographical distribution of the companies in the Global 500 rankings. Most of this growth is accounted for by a rapid increase in the number of Chinese Global 500 companies, of which there were 135 by 2021, increasing from only 10 in 2001. The share of [European](/wiki/Europe "Europe")-based companies declined, from 158 to 143, over the same period.[[2]](#cite_note-2)[[3]](#cite_note-3)[[4]](#cite_note-4)

Prince Henri was born on 16 April 1955, at the [Betzdorf Castle](/wiki/Betzdorf_Castle "Betzdorf Castle") in [Luxembourg](/wiki/Luxembourg "Luxembourg") as the second child and first son of [Jean, Hereditary Grand Duke of Luxembourg](/wiki/Jean,_Grand_Duke_of_Luxembourg "Jean, Grand Duke of Luxembourg"), and his wife, [Princess Joséphine-Charlotte of Belgium](/wiki/Princess_Jos%C3%A9phine-Charlotte_of_Belgium "Princess Joséphine-Charlotte of Belgium"). His father was the eldest son of [Charlotte, Grand Duchess of Luxembourg](/wiki/Charlotte,_Grand_Duchess_of_Luxembourg "Charlotte, Grand Duchess of Luxembourg"), and [Prince Félix of Bourbon-Parma](/wiki/Prince_F%C3%A9lix_of_Bourbon-Parma "Prince Félix of Bourbon-Parma"). His mother was the only daughter of King [Leopold III of Belgium](/wiki/Leopold_III_of_Belgium "Leopold III of Belgium") by his first wife, Princess [Astrid of Sweden](/wiki/Astrid_of_Sweden "Astrid of Sweden"). The prince's godparents were his maternal uncle the Prince of Liège (later [Albert II of Belgium](/wiki/Albert_II_of_Belgium "Albert II of Belgium")) and his paternal aunt [Princess Marie Gabriele](/wiki/Princess_Marie_Gabrielle_of_Luxembourg "Princess Marie Gabrielle of Luxembourg").

Henri has four siblings: [Archduchess Marie Astrid of Austria](/wiki/Archduchess_Marie_Astrid_of_Austria "Archduchess Marie Astrid of Austria") (born 1954), [Prince Jean of Luxembourg](/wiki/Prince_Jean_of_Luxembourg "Prince Jean of Luxembourg") (born 1957), [Princess Margaretha of Liechtenstein](/wiki/Princess_Margaretha_of_Liechtenstein "Princess Margaretha of Liechtenstein") (born 1957) and [Prince Guillaume of Luxembourg](/wiki/Prince_Guillaume_of_Luxembourg "Prince Guillaume of Luxembourg") (born 1963).

Land relief in Europe shows great variation within relatively small areas. The southern regions are more mountainous, while moving north the terrain descends from the high [Alps](/wiki/Alps "Alps"), [Pyrenees](/wiki/Pyrenees "Pyrenees") and [Carpathians](/wiki/Carpathians "Carpathians"), through hilly uplands, into broad, low northern plains, which are vast in the east. This extended lowland is known as the [Great European Plain](/wiki/Great_European_Plain "Great European Plain") and at its heart lies the [North German Plain](/wiki/North_German_Plain "North German Plain"). An arc of uplands also exists along the north-western seaboard, which begins in the western parts of the islands of Britain and Ireland, and then continues along the mountainous, [fjord](/wiki/Fjord "Fjord")-cut spine of Norway.
